label: Text 1
transcript: The class read three short speech excerpts from different decades and political camps: Lincoln's Gettysburg Address (1863), Margaret Thatcher's the lady's not for turning (1980), and a 2024 climate speech by a 17-year-old delegate at COP30. Mr. Yilmaz framed the question: what makes each of these technically effective, regardless of whether you agree with the content?

label: Text 2
transcript: Lincoln (1863): Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.

label: Text 3
transcript: Thatcher (1980): To those waiting with bated breath for that favourite media catchphrase, the U-turn, I have only one thing to say. You turn if you want to. The lady's not for turning.

label: Text 4
transcript: COP30 delegate (2024): I am seventeen. The policy you write today is the policy I am eighty-two years old in. I would like, accordingly, to be more than a footnote in this room.
